name: TASC SOLUM - Sequestration and Optimised Landscapes Using Microbials - VPA1
description: The Programme of Activities (PoA) “TASC SOLUM - Sequestration and Optimised Landscapes Using Microbials” aims to improve the health of agricultural land in South Africa by using natural biostimulants to enhance soil carbon sequestration. TASC is including this Voluntary Project Activity within the PoA. The main goal of the project is to remove carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere and store it permanently in agricultural soils, which is good for the environment and can help reduce the effects of climate change by decreasing greenhouse gas emissions (GHG).Current intensive and high-input forms of agriculture are leading to biodiversity loss, soil erosion, poor water retention, decreased drought resilience, GHG emissions, decreased plant health and nutrition, and decreased soil health. Applying regenerative agricultural practices addresses these issues via several ways, including precision application of biological and chemical inputs, minimising soil disturbance, inter-cropping, cover cropping, and integrating livestock when possible. This project within the regenerative agriculture programme will focus on the precision application of biological and chemical inputs.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: TASC SOLUM - Sequestration and Optimised Landscapes Using Microbials

name: GS12187 Biomass Briquettes at Kensalt
description:
The purpose of this Real VPA is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in industry in Kenya by reducing the use of energy from heavy fuel oil in the baseline by substituting it with renewable biomass briquettes, made from bagasse which is a waste stream from the sugar industry. Sugar is an annual crop and therefore renewable . The fuel oil in the baseline is deemed “non-renewable”. The main greenhouse gas being reduced by the project is carbon dioxide.  

More specifically, Tamuwa Limited (the Project Implementer) sells briquettes to Kensalt in 
Malindi that makes edible salt from sea water.

name: SPOUTS Distributed Technology Devices Program in Rwanda
description:
The purpose of the VPA is to disseminate Safe Water Supply (SWS) devices such as Institutional water treatment (IWT) and Household Water Treatment (HWT) technologies and Improved cookstoves in households and communities of Rwanda, Africa. The filters and/or Improved cookstoves are distributed to households/institutions which were earlier using wood and/or charcoal on rudimentary stoves for cooking/boiling or were consuming untreated water, for households where filters are distributed. The project makes the end-users energy efficient and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions otherwise resulting from the burning of non-renewable woody biomass and/or charcoal in baseline scenario. 
The project boundary is the geographical boundary of Rwanda, Africa where the water filters/Improved cookstoves are proposed to be distributed.

name: Idea Balance Safe Water Access Project
description:
The "Idea Balance Safe Water Access Project" will be implemented on Zanzibar Island, part of the United Republic of Tanzania. The project focuses on rehabilitating non-functional boreholes that have not received maintenance from the government or any authorized entity. These efforts will be financed and coordinated by the IDEA Universal International Development and Environment Association (IDEA Universal), leveraging their extensive expertise in sustainable water access initiatives.

This initiative aims to restore orphaned boreholes, identified based on household need and proximity to communities without alternative drinking water sources within a 1 km radius. By providing access to safe and clean drinking water, the project intends to reduce greenhouse gas emissions associated with boiling unsafe water and to decrease reliance on non-renewable biomass, mitigating environmental degradation and promoting sustainable resource use.

name: Swacch Hawa Chulho (Cookstove) Project in Nepal by Removall
description: The project aims to bring a positive impact in the livelihoods of project beneficiaries by disseminating improved cooking devices in Nepal. The project ICSs will replace traditional/inefficient biomass stoves currently used as baseline technologies. The prevalent use of such traditional cooking systems in Nepal results in significant greenhouse gas emissions from the use of non-renewable biomass (NRB), which is often sourced unsustainably. Additionally, traditional biomass-based cooking generates high levels of smoke and particulate matter (PM), exposing the primary cook—usually women—to hazardous indoor air pollution (IAP). The improved cookstoves (ICSs) introduced by the project are designed to be thermally more efficient, reducing fuel consumption, cooking time, and emissions. As a result, the project contributes to GHG emission reductions while also creating a cleaner cooking environment and reducing IAP exposure for women and children.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS12219 GS12220 RVPA-1 Global Household Water Treatment Technology dissemination project, Madhya Pradesh
description:
The regular case voluntary project activity (VPA) is providing household water filtration units for marginalized households in India living in rural, urban, semi-urban areas. The VPA is a part of POA and its real case VPA, which will contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gases and socio-economic progress for communities who are relying on unsafe drinking water sources and thus the objective of the VPA is to disseminate household water treatment units in Madhya Pradesh, India so that the rural communities living in remote hilly areas have increased access of safe drinking water for their daily use and thus increased living standard for the poor and marginalized people. 
The regular case VPA under the GS Programme of Activity provides safe household drinking water treatment solutions to marginalized households at free of cost and replace the usage of equivalent quantity of fuel wood in traditional three stone fire or any other conventional wood stoves which are inefficient and smoke-intensive and which would have been used to boil the water to make it safe for drinking purposes.

name: Restore Africa: Restoring Landscapes and Livelihoods in Western Kenya and Rift Valley
description:
The Restore Africa: Restoring Landscapes and Livelihoods in Western Kenya and Rift Valley Kenya project is implemented in Kenya’s Elgeyo-Marakwet, Migori and Narok counties. Over several decades, these counties have experienced substantial deforestation and degradation because of poor agricultural practices, overgrazing and unsustainable demand for fuelwood. The scenario - the continued degradation of land and erosion of livelihood opportunities – will most likely continue to occur unless there is a substantial and additional intervention
The project focuses on establishment of new trees (e.g. through manual planting and broadcast seeding) as well as the improved management activities that enhance the natural regeneration of established root stock (e.g. through coppice management) in the Elgeyo-Marakwet, Migori and Narok counties in Kenya, involving more than 75,000 small farmer households. The aim is to both sequester carbon as well as generate a broad set of environmental and socio-economic co-benefits through the implementation of sustainable agroforestry practices at a landscape scale. Co-benefits, based on the restoration of ecosystem functions, include increased household income, enhanced local livelihoods, increased gender equality and the improvement of ecosystem services.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Restore Africa: Restoring Landscapes and Livelihoods in Coastal Kenya
description:
The Restore Africa: Restoring Landscapes and Livelihoods in Coastal Kenya project is implemented in Kenya’s coastal region, specifically in the Kwale and Kilifi counties. With an annual deforestation rate of 0.58%, Kenya faces significant forest loss, primarily driven by dependence on natural resources and extensive land degradation.  The primary causes of land degradation include unsustainable wood resource exploitation, the expansion of unsustainable cultivation practices, the spread of invasive species, pollution, and climate change.
The project focuses on establishment of new trees (e.g. through manual planting and broadcast seeding) as well as the improved management activities that enhance the natural regeneration of established root stock (e.g. through coppice management) in the Kwale and Kilifi counties in Kenya, involving more than 100,000 small farmer households. The aim is to both sequester carbon as well as generate a broad set of environmental and socio-economic co-benefits through the implementation of sustainable agroforestry practices at a landscape scale. Co-benefits, based on the restoration of ecosystem functions, include increased household income, enhanced local livelihoods, increased gender equality and the improvement of ecosystem services.
The project builds on extensive experience in socio-economic development within the region.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Restore Africa: Restoring Landscapes and Livelihoods in Malawi
description:
The Restore Africa: Restoring Landscapes and Livelihoods in Malawi project is implemented in degraded agricultural landscapes in the in the Northern, Central and Southern Regions of the country. Over 90% of households in the country depend on natural resources and subsistence agriculture to meet their livelihoods, food and energy needs. Extensive clearing of forest and woodlands for fuelwood, followed by conversion to cropland, is driving a high annual deforestation rate of 1%.
The project focuses on establishment of new trees (e.g. through manual planting and broadcast seeding) as well as the improved management activities that enhance the natural regeneration of established root stock (e.g. through coppice management) in seven districts in Malawi involving more than 150,000 small farmer households. The aim is to both sequester carbon as well as generate a broad set of environmental and socio-economic co-benefits through the implementation of sustainable agroforestry practices at a landscape scale. Co-benefits, based on the restoration of ecosystem functions, include sustainable food production, enhanced local livelihoods, increased gender equality and the improvement of ecosystem services.
The project will collaborate and align with the many organizations already established in the area to enhance long-term sustainability and ensure that implementation occurs in an efficient, locally appropriate, and acceptable manner.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Restore Africa: Restoring Landscapes and Livelihoods in Western Uganda
description:
The Restore Africa: Restoring Landscapes and Livelihoods in Western Uganda project is implemented in degraded agricultural landscapes in the Western (Afromontane) highlands and pastoral rangelands of mid-Western Uganda. Over several decades, these regions have experienced substantial deforestation and degradation, poor agriculture practices, overgrazing, and an unsustainable demand for fuelwood. Climate change, population increases, poverty and lack of economic opportunities further exacerbate pressure on the land. 
The project focuses on establishment of new trees (e.g. through manual planting and broadcast seeding) as well as the improved management activities that enhance the natural regeneration of established root stock (e.g. through coppice management) in 24 districts in Western Uganda involving more than 200,000 small farmer households. The aim is to both sequester carbon as well as generate a broad set of environmental and socio-economic co-benefits through the implementation of sustainable agroforestry practices at a landscape scale. Co-benefits, based on the restoration of ecosystem functions, include sustainable food production, enhanced local livelihoods, increased gender equality and the improvement of ecosystem services.
The project will collaborate and align with the many organizations already established in the area to enhance long-term sustainability and ensure that implementation occurs in an efficient, locally appropriate, and acceptable manner.

name: Enabling Clean Energy Transitions Through BESS Integration
description: The project involves the deployment of a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) to store electricity generated from renewable energy sources such as solar or wind. The BESS enables time-shifting of renewable energy by storing surplus electricity during periods of low demand and discharging it during peak demand periods or grid stress events. This reduces the need for fossil fuel-based peaking power plants and supports grid stability and renewable energy integration. The system comprises battery, power conversion systems (inverters), battery management systems, and control software to optimize charging/discharging cycles. The project contributes to greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions by displacing grid electricity that would otherwise be generated from fossil fuels.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Healthy Kitchens and Happy Lives in Africa
description:
SDG13 Ventures aims to implement this Program of Activities (PoA) to enhance access to clean cooking solutions across multiple Sub-Saharan African countries. 
The initiative aims to replace traditional three-stone firewood stoves with improved biomass cookstoves/high efficiency electric stoves in rural and semi-urban
households, providing better access to cleaner energy and technology. By scaling up the distribution of these cookstoves, the project will directly benefit women from impoverished communities with limited economic resources. This collective effort seeks to deliver sustainable solutions that enhance rural livelihoods while addressing critical health, environmental, and socio-economic challenges.
